name: Georgia

jury_list.statute: O.C.G.A. 21-2-231(a.1): each superior court clerk sends the Secretary of State, by the tenth day of each month, a list of all persons 'who identify themselves as not being citizens of the United States during their qualification to serve as a juror'. No statute making the list public was found.
jury_list.official_pipeline: Superior court clerks report self-identified non-citizen jurors monthly to the Secretary of State (21-2-231(a.1)). The Secretary sends names on the list of electors to the county board of registrars, which removes them and mails a notice (21-2-231(c)(1)). Registrars must act within 60 days (21-2-231(f)).

sources.cite: O.C.G.A. 21-2-231 - Justia copy of the 2025 Georgia Code

Georgia Department of Audits and Accounts, Voter Registration and List Maintenance (lists 'Superior Court Clerk: Non-citizens identified through juror qualification' as a 21-2-231 data source; SOS citizenship audits 2024 to April 2026 used juror affidavits of non-citizenship, DDS data and SAVE)
Georgia Secretary of State, Qualifications for Electors (quotes O.C.G.A. 21-2-231(c)(1) on lists under (a.1))

voter_file.who_may_get: Any person, by purchase from the Secretary of State (per the Secretary of State's official order page and online store).
voter_file.permitted_uses: Any use except commercial purposes: 'Such data may not be used by any person for commercial purposes' (O.C.G.A. 21-2-225(c)).
voter_file.penalty: Misdemeanor for intentional commercial use of the list of electors (O.C.G.A. 21-2-601).

sources.cite: Georgia Secretary of State online store - Voter List (contents: name, residential and mailing address, race, gender, registration date, last voting date; no date of birth; 21-2-225(c) and 21-2-601 notices)
O.C.G.A. 21-2-225(b)-(c) (public data; month and day of birth confidential; year of birth public; no commercial use) - Justia copy of the 2025 Georgia Code
O.C.G.A. 21-2-601 (misdemeanor for commercial use) - Justia copy of the 2025 Georgia Code

private_challenge.who: Any elector of the county or municipality (O.C.G.A. 21-2-229(a), 21-2-230(a)).
private_challenge.form_or_statute: O.C.G.A. 21-2-229 (challenge to qualifications to remain on the list; hearing by the board of registrars) and 21-2-230 (challenge to the right to vote in an election; probable-cause review). Written challenge that specifies the grounds, filed with the county board of registrars.
private_challenge.deadlines: 21-2-229: hearing set within 10 business days after notice; appeal to superior court within 10 days. 21-2-230: before the challenged elector votes (absentee: before 5:00 p.m. the day before scanning starts); any challenge within 45 days of a primary, runoff or election is postponed until certification (21-2-230(b)(1), SB 189 (2024)).
private_challenge.evidence_standard: 21-2-229(c): burden on the challenging elector to prove the person is not qualified. 21-2-230(b): registrars must find probable cause or deny the challenge.

sources.cite: Georgia SB 189 (2024), Section 5 - amended O.C.G.A. 21-2-230(b) (probable cause; 45-day postponement)
Georgia SB 202 (2021), Sections 15-16 - O.C.G.A. 21-2-229 and 21-2-230 ('There shall not be a limit on the number of persons whose qualifications such elector may challenge.')

state_windows.effect: Postponed until certification of the primary, election or runoff is complete.

county_board.name: County election offices / boards of registrars (Georgia Secretary of State directory)

state_election_office.name: Georgia Secretary of State - Elections Division

gates.basis: No source found that makes the juror non-citizen list available to a private person (jury_list.public is null, so the strict default applies). Without a lawful jury list there are no named leads. Aggregate audit mode only: ask officials whether the 21-2-231(a.1) monthly reports are filed and processed.

notes: The official pipeline already exists: clerks report monthly to the Secretary of State (21-2-231(a.1)). The best private action is an aggregate referral that asks whether each county files and processes these reports.

Source status: 21-2-229 and 21-2-230 were read from enrolled session laws (SB 202 of 2021, SB 189 of 2024) on gov.georgia.gov. 21-2-231, 21-2-225 and 21-2-601 were re-read on 2026-10-07 from the Justia copy of the 2025 Georgia Code, the source LEGAL-REVIEW steering allows for GA. The text matches the earlier official-page summaries.
UNVERIFIED, not relied on: a secondary summary says HB 397 (2025-2026 session) did not add new challenge rules (proposed 21-2-230.1). No rule value uses it. Re-check against the enrolled act.
The public voter list has no date of birth. If the jury gate ever opens in GA, matches would be capped at Probable (LOGIC-CHANGES.md A.4).

Federal cases: Majority Forward v. Ben Hill County, 512 F. Supp. 3d 1354 (M.D. Ga. 2021) (mass private challenges in the 90-day window need individualized inquiry); Fair Fight v. True the Vote (N.D. Ga. 2024) (about 364,000 challenges; list 'utterly lacking reliability') (LEGAL-REVIEW.md).
